job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: During the school football match, Rohan twisted his ankle while dribbling. His coach, Mr. Sharma, immediately stopped the game and told Rohan to sit down. Rohan wanted to keep playing, claiming he could walk it off, but Mr. Sharma insisted that playing through pain often worsens an injury. He explained that a sprain involves stretched ligaments, not just a simple muscle strain. To manage the swelling, Mr. Sharma applied an ice pack to the ankle rather than heat, as heat increases blood flow and inflammation. He wrapped the ankle with a bandage, but warned Rohan not to pull it too tight, as it needs to allow proper circulation. Rohan felt better after ten minutes and asked if he could return to the field. Mr. Sharma shook his head, noting that the absence of immediate pain does not mean the injury has fully healed. He also reminded the team that a concussion can occur even without losing consciousness, so any head bump requires a doctor's check. Finally, he advised Rohan to keep his ankle elevated above heart level to reduce throbbing. Rohan realized that recovery requires patience, proper first aid, and professional advice rather than just rushing back to the game.

items.evidence: Rohan wanted to keep playing, claiming he could walk it off, but Mr. Sharma insisted that playing through pain often worsens an injury.
items.q: Why did Mr. Sharma refuse to let Rohan keep playing on the hurt ankle?
options: Continuing could make the damage greater
Walking would tire the other leg
The pain would stop and heal it
Tough players must rest before a match
items.explain: Playing through pain often worsens an injury, so the coach made Rohan stop.

wrong.why: thinks pain going away means healing
mixes up toughness with the right response to injury

items.evidence: He explained that a sprain involves stretched ligaments, not just a simple muscle strain.
items.q: Rohan twisted his ankle badly. Which injury does the coach say he has?
options: Stretched ligaments at the joint
A torn muscle in the leg
A bone cracked inside the ankle
A strain of the thigh muscle
items.explain: A sprain means stretched ligaments at a joint, which is different from a muscle strain.

wrong.why: thinks a sprain is a muscle injury
thinks a swollen joint must have a broken bone

items.evidence: To manage the swelling, Mr. Sharma applied an ice pack to the ankle rather than heat, as heat increases blood flow and inflammation.
items.q: What would most likely happen if heat were put on Rohan's fresh sprain?
options: The swelling would grow worse
The swelling would go down faster
The ankle would heal in minutes
The swelling would stay the same
items.explain: Heat increases blood flow and inflammation, so a fresh sprain would swell more.

wrong.why: thinks warmth quickly heals the injury

items.evidence: He wrapped the ankle with a bandage, but warned Rohan not to pull it too tight, as it needs to allow proper circulation.
items.q: Rohan says a very tight bandage will work best. Why is he wrong?
options: Blood must still be able to flow
Tight bandages slip off during play
Bandages only work when worn loosely
Ice cannot reach through a tight wrap
items.explain: The bandage must allow proper circulation, so wrapping it too tight is harmful.

wrong.why: believes a tighter bandage works better
picks a nearby detail that is not the reason
thinks the wrap only matters as part of RICE

items.evidence: He also reminded the team that a concussion can occur even without losing consciousness, so any head bump requires a doctor's check.
items.q: Asha bumps her head in a game but stays awake. What should happen?
options: A doctor should check her for concussion
She is safe because she stayed awake
She should walk it off and keep playing
She should wait for symptoms to show
items.explain: A concussion can happen without losing consciousness, so any head bump needs a doctor's check.

wrong.why: thinks you should play through it
